headline: Canadian detentions in US rise 60 percent despite 25 percent drop in travel
snippet: Global Affairs Canada reported on Thursday that the number of Canadian citizens arrested or detained in the United States increased by 60 percent during the fiscal year ending in March 2026. The annual consular report details 557 such cases in the U. S., up from 361 in the previous year, while noting that the total number of Canadian visits to the U. S. dropped by 25 percent over the same period. The report does not attribute specific causes to the rise in detentions, though it coincides with a period of intensified immigration enforcement under the U. S. administration. The data distinguishes between the frequency of cross-border travel and the legal consequences faced by those present in the U. S. territory. While 20 million Canadians traveled to the United States between April 2025 and March 2026-a decrease from 26.8 million in the prior year-instances of arrest or detention rose sharply. This divergence suggests that the risk is no longer tied solely to volume of travel but to specific enforcement mechanisms targeting individuals already within the U. S. or those entering with minor infractions. Enforcement Practices and Legal Exposure Len Saunders, an immigration lawyer based in Blaine, Washington, adjacent to the Canadian border, identified a shift in how U. S. authorities handle Canadian residents. He stated that many of his clients are not temporary visitors but long-term residents holding green cards or permanent resident status who are now facing deportation proceedings. Saunders noted that these individuals often have deep roots in the U. S., including U. S. citizen spouses or children and receipt of American pensions. According to Saunders, some clients believed they were legally resident until receiving contact from U. S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents.

headline: Trump’s fresh bid for Nobel Peace Prize
snippet: Washington, Oct 08: US President Donald Trump has made a fresh bid for the Nobel Peace Prize, claiming that he had settled eight wars and “done stuff that nobody else has ever done”. Trump made the remarks at the Oval Office on Wednesday afternoon, ahead of the announcement of the coveted award on Friday by the Norwegian Peace Committee. “I’ve done stuff that nobody else has ever done. I’m not bragging, I’m just telling you the facts. No president has probably ever settled any wars. I settled eight wars," Trump told reporters here. The US President said it would be a great discredit to the Nobel Committee not to honour him. “They have a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me. But, whether I get it or not, I have done far more. And I think it would be a great discredit to them. And I'm not saying that out of scorn, I'm saying that when you settle eight wars, and nobody’s never,” Trump said. The US President said his peacemaking efforts were continuing and indicated that he was on course to settle another war, an apparent reference to the US-Iran war that has now stretched into its eighth month. Trump said he deserved the award more than President Barack Obama, whom he accused of not knowing why he had received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2009. “Look, Obama got it, and he didn't do anything. He still doesn't know what he got it for. He got it when he got elected, right at the beginning, and he had no idea why he got it,” the US President said. Trump recalled that last year’s peace laureate Venezuela’s Maria Corina Machado had handed over her prize to him at the Oval Office. “Last time they gave it to a young lady who's a fabulous person, and she said she didn't deserve it, that I deserved it, and she gave it to me,” the US President said. “I was very honoured to receive it indirectly. Last time by the recipient, who said nobody in history deserves it more than President Trump,” he said. Trump repeated that in the past year he had settled eight wars, secured the return of all hostages, and prevented many wars by using the power of tariffs as a threat against certain countries, thereby stopping them from killing people.
